slides.sub: The Croydon kid who built dubstep. And left it behind.

text: At 11, he broke into his brother's room.
slides.sub: Croydon, 1997. His name was Oliver Jones. He didn't know he was about to invent something.

text: He skipped school to be here.
slides.sub: A record shop where dubstep was still a feeling — not a name yet. Hatcha played his first dubs. The scene was a room before it became a movement.
Wiley called it perfect. Ricardo Villalobos played it in his minimal techno sets.
The Stella Sessions. Rinse FM. Every week. Live. No script.

text: Three producers from the same Croydon block.
slides.sub: Magnetic Man. Columbia Records. 'I Need Air' ft. Katy B. UK Top 10. Dubstep was on the radio. And something was ending.

quote: It doesn't have a meaning anymore.
slides.note: 2012. He was 26. He walked off the dubstep stage. Stepped into a different booth. House. Disco. 120 BPM. A different kind of dark.

text: Then something else takes its name.
The only way to keep going
